ready1_open_rewrite.title: MM-Math open-ended problem
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: The cross-section of a drainpipe is shown in the figure below. Given that the radius of the drainpipe is $OB=10$, and the width of the water surface $AB=12$. If more water is added, such that the width of the water surface $AB$ changes to $16$, then by how much does the height of the water surface $AB$ increase?
ready1_open_rewrite.expected_answer: \textbf{Solution:} Given $EF \parallel AB$, $EF=16$. Draw $OC \perp AB$ at point $C$, intersecting $EF$ at point $G$. Connect $OE$. $\therefore OC \perp EF$, $\therefore \angle OGE=\angle OCB=90^\circ$, $BC=\frac{1}{2}AB=6$, $EG=\frac{1}{2}EF=8$, In $\triangle OCB$, $OC=\sqrt{OB^{2}-CB^{2}}=\sqrt{10^{2}-6^{2}}=8$; In $\triangle EOG$, $OG=\sqrt{OE^{2}-EG^{2}}=\sqrt{10^{2}-8^{2}}=6$ When $EF$ and $AB$ are on the same side of the center $O$, $CG=OC-OG=8-6=2$; When $EF$ and $AB$ are on opposite sides of the center $O$, $CG=OC+OG=8+6=14$; $\therefore$ When the width of the water surface $AB$ changes to 16, the height by which the water surface $AB$ rises is $\boxed{2}$ or 14

Drop the perpendicular from O to AB at C and extend it to meet EF at G. Use the circle theorem that a perpendicular from the center to a chord bisects the chord, so BC=6 and EG=8. Apply the Pythagorean theorem in right triangles OCB and OGE to get OC=sqrt(10^2-6^2)=8 and OG=sqrt(10^2-8^2)=6. If the new water surface EF and the original water surface AB are on the same side of the center O, that is, still below the center of the circle, then the rise height CG=OC-OG=8-6=2. If the new water surface EF has already crossed the center of the circle to the other side, then the rise height CG=OC+OG=8+6=14. Therefore the possible rise height is 2 or 14.
